question: Should OpenClaw expose `preemptiveOverflowRatio` and `maxOverflowAttempts` as supported persistent agent-default configuration, rather than keep overflow tuning internal?
rationale: The patch creates two new long-lived public configuration knobs; deciding whether these controls belong in the supported config contract cannot be resolved mechanically from the stale branch.

options.title: Approve the knobs with a refreshed implementation
options.body: Accept the config contract, then require a rebase onto the active runner and public documentation before merge.

options.title: Keep tuning internal
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and close the related requests unless a narrower supported control is specified.

options.title: Choose a narrower supported control
options.body: Define one consolidated compaction headroom or retry policy instead of exposing both low-level knobs.

recommendation.title: Approve the knobs with a refreshed implementation
recommendation.body: Accept the config contract, then require a rebase onto the active runner and public documentation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The paired reports contain the concrete operational rationale, though a core agent-runtime owner should make the final product decision.
